items.title: Israeli occupiers injure palestinians near jerusalem, seize west bank home
items.summary: The Jerusalem Governorate said Israeli occupiers backed by Israeli forces attacked residents of the Al-Arara Bedouin community near Jaba, assaulting several Palestinians. It added that Israeli forces prevented ambulance crews from reaching the injured. Local sources also said that Israeli occupiers hurled stones at Palestinian vehicles near the Jaba roundabout, damaging several cars.

items.title: France and Spain race to contain fires before new heatwave
items.summary: NAVALUENGA, Spain: President Emmanuel Macron on Monday said one forest fire in southwest France had been "contained" even as another, much bigger one near Bordeaux continued to rage, and western Europe braced for new heatwaves this week. The return of searing temperatures, from Tuesday in France and from Wednesday in Spain, threaten to complicate fire-fighting efforts. Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said the coming hours would be "absolutely decisive" to bring fires burning west of the capital, Madrid, under control.

items.title: [WATCH] Fire damages fuel price signboard at BHP petrol station in Kuala Lumpur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A fire broke out at a BHP petrol station along the North-South Expressway near Sungai Besi last night, setting its fuel price signboard ablaze. "The fire engine arrived at 10.06pm and found that the blaze involved the station's fuel price signboard. View on Threads The operation involved five firefighters and a fire engine.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson announces US$5.5bil settlement of talc lawsuits
items.summary: NEW YORK: Johnson & Johnson said (J&J) on Monday it would pay US$5.5 billion to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits alleging its baby powder and other talc products cause ovarian cancer, in a landmark settlement aimed at closing a chapter of contentious litigation that has dogged the company for years. J&J said the settlement covers about 69,000 cases consolidated in federal court in New Jersey, and related cases in state court, totaling 99.75 per cent of the remaining talc claims. J&J's vice president of litigation, Erik Haas, said the claims were "meritless" and that the company was willing to settle in order to get closure.

items.title: Chinese tech firms, from Apple suppliers to OpenAI rivals, raise US$27.13bil in Hong Kong
items.summary: NEW YORK: From robotaxi developers to AI startups and chipmakers, Chinese technology firms are flocking to Hong Kong's booming capital markets, raising a combined HKUS$212.75 billion (US$27.13 billion) this year to fund expansion in AI, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing. Dajin Heavy Industry In June, the wind power equipment maker set the offer price for its Hong Kong listing at HKUS$66.40 a share, aiming to raise HKUS$5.77 billion. Huaqin The smart device maker raised HKUS$4.6 billion in a Hong Kong share offering in April.

items.title: 38 early voting centres for N9 polls opened at 8am
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A total of 38 early voting centres for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election opened at 8 am today to allow 22,339 security forces personnel and their spouses to cast their ballots. According to statistics from the Election Commission (EC), 16,884 members of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) along with their spouses will cast their votes at eight designated polling centres. This Saturday, approximately 889,490 ordinary voters will determine the mandate in the 36-seat Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly.

items.title: Three killed, toddler among four wounded in Seattle shooting
items.summary: SEATTLE: A shooting near the Space Needle landmark in Seattle killed three people on Sunday and wounded at least four others including a toddler, officials said. Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said shots were heard around 6pm (0100 GMT) and "there were two people who we believe were shooting at each other." Seattle Police said two people died at the scene at the Seattle Center and a third died in hospital.

items.title: Young voters weigh candidates' track records ahead of Negri Sembilan polls
items.summary: Young voter K. Sasvini, 19, said she searched for information on candidates contesting the Sikamat state seat through the Election Commission's website. "I also looked up the candidates' backgrounds and track records on social media and the internet to choose the right candidate. Sasvini said she was excited to vote for the first time as she wanted to fulfil her responsibility of electing a representative for her constituency.

items.title: Lax enforcement, coordination: Recurring floods expose Petaling Jaya's weaknesses [WATCH]
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Sivasangari Rama Rago buried her husband last August. The real question isn't why Petaling Jaya floods — it's why, after decades of committees and press statements, it floods exactly the same way, every time. The Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) has admitted this itself.

items.title: AMRO lifts Asean+3 growth forecast as AI demand boosts regional resilience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Asean+3 region's economic growth forecast has been revised upward to 4.1 per cent for 2026 from the previous projection of 4.0 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand, strong technology exports and sustained momentum in the artificial intelligence (AI) sector. The Asean+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO), in its July 2026 Quarterly Update of the Asean+3 Regional Economic Outlook (AREO) released yesterday, said growth is expected to ease slightly to 4.0 per cent in 2027. Headline inflation is now projected at 1.6 per cent in 2026, compared with the earlier forecast of 1.8 per cent, reflecting lower global commodity price assumptions.

items.title: RM58 billion growth push to support economic growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Economy Ministry seeks to allocate RM58 billion, or 70 per cent of the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) 2027 development expenditure, for basic development projects to ensure the continuity of ongoing initiatives, sustain economic growth momentum and accelerate national development amid a challenging global environment. Basic development expenditure covers core public investments in physical infrastructure and essential services, including roads, schools, healthcare facilities, water supply, flood mitigation and other strategic projects. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said maintaining a strong allocation for basic development would ensure the continuity of strategic projects, support regional development and accelerate the country's physical infrastructure.

items.title: Iraq opens probe into Saudi drone attack claim
items.summary: BAGHDAD: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on Monday for an investigation into Saudi Arabia's claim that drones targeting its territory had been launched by pro-Iran groups in Iraq, his spokesman said. Zaidi directed "the competent security authorities to investigate the statement issued by the ministry of defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia regarding the targeting of the kingdom with drones launched from Iraqi territory", spokesman Sabah al-Numan said in a statement. The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, an umbrella network of Iran-backed Shia militias conducting attacks against US and Israeli targets while operating outside Iraq's formal military structure, said the Saudi accusations were "fabrications that serve only as an attempt to justify their inability to respond to the painful Yemeni strikes."

items.title: Trump touts economy, attacks Democrats in Michigan campaign-style speech
items.summary: MILFORD, Michigan: US President Donald Trump touted his record on investment, job creation and tax cuts on Monday less than 100 days before the November elections, even as polls showed Americans increasingly souring on his handling of the economy. In a campaign-style speech at a General Motors test facility in Michigan, Trump also lashed out at Democrats seeking to end Republican control of Congress, calling his political opponents "communists" to cheers from many in the audience. Michigan is thriving.

items.title: N9 Polls: Early voters cast ballots today
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A total of 22,339 military and police personnel and their spouses will cast their ballots today in the early voting for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election. Of the total, 16,884 are military personnel and their spouses, while 5,455 are police personnel and their spouses. The state election will see contest for 36 seats, involving 103 candidates.

items.title: Foreigner in extortion case involving 12 cops held over passport offences
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR The foreigner who was allegedly extorted by 12 Kuala Lumpur policemen was arrested along with his two female accomplices from Thailand and China, police said. Police sources said the 30-year-old man, who claimed he was extorted, had been travelling on a Vanuatu passport but checks with the Chinese embassy confirmed he was also their citizen. The Vanuatu consular-general in Kuala Lumpur, Henry Savarimuthu, told the New Straits Times the man had not approached the consulate for any help so far.

items.title: Stability, change among key factors shaping Negri Sembilan election [WATCH]
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional has denied claims of any quarrel or disagreement with Perikatan Nasional, insisting that both coalitions continue to work together based on mutual understanding. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said differing views expressed previously were the result of varying circumstances in different states and should not be construed as a sign of a strained relationship. We are moving forward together based on mutual understanding.

items.title: New Sirim certification to combat fake engine oils
items.summary: In a move against the proliferation of counterfeit engine oils, Sirim QAS International Sdn Bhd has officially rolled out the SIRIM 58 Standard — Certification Scheme for Genuine Products (Engine Oil for Motor Vehicles). For years, counterfeit engine oils have posed a growing and complex challenge to consumers and the automotive industry. "Through the Certification Scheme for Genuine Product, consumers have a trusted and convenient way to verify product authenticity before use."

items.title: Houthis pushing to model Iran's Hormuz control in Red Sea: Yemen
items.summary: RIYADH: Yemen's Houthi Movement aims to replicate Iran's Hormuz Strait strategy in the Red Sea by disrupting shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb and has been emboldened by an insufficient international response, Yemen's top diplomat said on Monday. The Red Sea has become a new front in the Iran war, with the Houthis taking an escalatory approach against Saudi Arabia by firing missiles and drones at the kingdom and declaring a blockade on Saudi shipping. Saudi Arabia has responded with airstrikes on what it said were Houthi military facilities and said it would protect commercial shipping, accusing the Houthis of serving foreign agendas.

items.title: What would you do if food deliveries, e-hailing prices go up in Malaysia? 82pc surveyed say will reduce or stop using
items.summary: In consumer research company Rakuten Insight’s latest survey, 82 per cent of the 1,003 Malaysian respondents said they would change their behaviours (including reducing or not using these services) if ride-hailing or food delivery prices continue to rise due to fuel costs. For example, 28 per cent said they would switch to cheaper alternatives such as public transport, driving themselves, or cooking at home; 27 per cent said they would use such services less often; 17 per cent would only use when there is a promotion, while 10 per cent would stop using such services altogether. In the July edition of the survey known as the Malaysia Cost Pressure Pulse (MCPP), only eight per cent said they would continue using these services as usual, as they say it is worth it for the convenience.

items.title: Four killed in Bentong crash covered by Perkeso's Lindung 24 Jam scheme
items.summary: Perkeso said the case underscored the importance of extending social security coverage beyond working hours. Perkeso said V. Mugilan, A. Kanabati Raja, K. Alaganathan and M. Parathanman, aged between 16 and 25, were active contributors covered under the Employees' Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4). Kanabati Raja's family will receive monthly dependants' benefits of RM1,647, while Parathanman's dependants will receive RM891 a month.

items.title: NUTP backs use of military veterans as school wardens
items.summary: Its president, Aminuddin Awang, said the Education Ministry's biggest challenge was managing nearly 1,900 boarding schools nationwide. Aminuddin said NUTP had for years advocated appointing dedicated full-time wardens at all boarding schools. What matters is having full-time wardens at boarding schools, especially fully residential schools.

items.title: Malaysia's rich shift into protection mode
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Affluent and high-net-worth investors in Malaysia are focused on building wealth buffers to offset inflation, according to the HSBC Affluent Investor Snapshot. Beyond building wealth, investors are focused on preserving it and preparing for retirement. The survey showed that affluent and high-net-worth investors in Malaysia are moving cash more actively than their global peers.

items.title: Trump sees Iran deal despite fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: TEHERAN: US President Donald Trump on Monday voiced optimism at the prospects for a negotiated peace deal with Iran, as the two sides held their fire for a third consecutive day. Fighting between the longtime foes has been paused since Friday after 13 nights of renewed US strikes on the Islamic republic sparked by a breakdown in diplomacy over Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. "I have a lot of patience... We'll see what happens," he said aboard Air Force One.

items.title: Yemen prepared for any escalations with Houthis
items.summary: RIYADH: Yemen's internationally recognised government on Monday said it is ready for any escalation with Houthi rebels after the Iran-backed group launched attacks and a maritime blockade targeting Saudi Arabia. Fears are growing that renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels in Yemen may further destabilise the Arabian peninsula and rattle the region's precarious fault lines. Last week, the Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and have claimed attacks targeting Saudi tankers and oil infrastructure in the kingdom.

items.title: Man claiming police extorted him wanted by Interpol over scam case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A foreigner who lodged a police report alleging he was extorted by individuals believed to be the police is now under investigation after checks with the International Criminal Police Organisation (Interpol) found he was wanted in China over a fraud case. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks revealed that the man was not a Vanuatu national as initially claimed, but was believed to be a Chinese citizen. Following the report, police arrested 15 police officers believed to be linked to the case.

items.title: El Nino: Johor, Melaka face up to 40 per cent less rainfall
items.summary: Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the east coast of Sabah could also experience reduced rainfall due to its location closer to the Pacific Ocean. However, he said states along the east coast and northern parts of the Peninsula were not expected to experience significant effects until the end of the year, based on six-month projections. Hisham said the Northeast Monsoon typically begins in late October or early November and ends in late March, with east coast states usually receiving the highest rainfall in November and December.

items.title: Four trucks take hundreds of Rohingya from UNHCR office to KL police HQ
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hundreds of Rohingya refugees who gathered outside the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Jalan Bukit Petaling here yesterday were moved to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters for documentation and identity verification. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus, when contacted, confirmed that all the foreign nationals had been transferred to the police headquarters. Checks at the scene found that the transfer operation began at 8.20pm, using four police trucks after the two vehicles initially deployed proved insufficient as many of the refugees were carrying luggage and personal belongings.

items.title: 'Coolcations' gather pace as European holidaymakers flee Mediterranean heat
items.summary: EUROPEAN holidaymakers worn down by recurrent heatwaves are snubbing Mediterranean destinations for northern climes in hopes of cooler temperatures, but it remains to be seen whether it is just a fad or a durable shift in the tourism market. With temperatures in the European summer regularly climbing up towards 40°C, cool has become cool. "We're happy to have found cooler temperatures," they said.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: Police probe video touching on royal institution
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan police have opened an investigation after receiving 11 reports over a TikTok video allegedly containing statements by a political party relating to the state's royal institution. State police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said investigators are examining the video's content and the context of the speech under Section 4(1) of the Election Offences Act 1954, Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. Alzafny also reminded all parties to use social media responsibly and avoid making statements touching on race, religion and the royal institution (3R) that could cause anxiety or tension among the public.

items.title: Petronas clarifies role in Sepang International Circuit, F1 ticket sales
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) has clarified that while it holds the naming rights to the Petronas Sepang International Circuit (SIC), the circuit itself is owned by Sepang International Circuit Sdn Bhd, a company under Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOF Inc). The national oil company said the circuit is operated by an agency under the Youth and Sports Ministry. Petronas issued the clarification following public interest surrounding the upcoming Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (Bahrain GP), scheduled to take place at SIC from Oct 2 to 4, 2026.

items.title: Burnham announces sweeteners in first week of office
items.summary: NEW United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham's first week in office signalled a shift in focus and style for the centre-left Labour government as he sought a clean break from predecessor Keir Starmer. Burnham's early sweeteners are raising questions about whether he shares Starmer's commitment to fiscal discipline, although he insists they represent a "re-prioritisation" of spending. On Friday, Burnham opened his new No.

items.title: ‘Reach for the sky, stay anchored to earth’: PM warns against tech without morals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on the public to keep pace with rapid technological advancements, while cautioning against adopting modern innovations at the expense of moral values. In his closing speech during the International Waqaf Dakwah Convention 2026 in KLCC, Anwar said that it is imperative especially in the education sector to be able to adapt to the rapid evolution of technology nowadays. “However, ‘reaching for the sky’ has its dangers, because AI, new technology, information technology, quantum computing - without values and morals, will erode humanity as well as moral and ethics.

items.title: TNB, Air Selangor sign agreements to strengthen critical infrastructure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 27 —Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor) today signed an Electricity Supply Agreement (ESA) and a Cooling Energy Supply Agreement (CESA) to strengthen the reliability, resilience and sustainability of the nation’s energy and water infrastructure. Under the ESA, TNB will supply high-voltage electricity to the Sungai Rasau Water Treatment Plant in Kuala Langat, Selangor, the largest water treatment plant in South-East Asia, with a treatment capacity of 1,400 million litres per day (MLD). In a joint statement today, TNB and Air Selangor said the plant, upon full completion in 2031, is expected to supply clean and safe treated water to 9.62 million consumers in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.

items.title: PM Anwar: No compromise on refugees violating laws, disturbing public order
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27—The government will not compromise with any group of refugees that violates the law, disrupts public order or attempts to take over any area in the country, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said enforcement agencies, including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Immigration Department (JIM) and local authorities (PBT), had been instructed to take firm action against any party that breached the law. Commenting on the gathering of hundreds of Rohingya refugees in front of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office at Jalan Bukit Petaling here today, Anwar stressed that everyone must respect the laws in force in the country.

items.title: PM Anwar urges JPKK leaders to uphold integrity and unity at grassroots level
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 27 — Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) leaders must carry out their responsibilities with integrity while providing the people with clear and accurate information on the government's initiatives and achievements, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Being at the grassroots, he said JPKK leaders also play a vital role in preserving racial harmony, strengthening national unity and safeguarding the country's stability and security. To strengthen the role and welfare of JPKK at the grassroots, the Prime Minister said the government has allocated RM5.319 million specifically for the committees in Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Senate passes competition bill to strengthen fight against cartels, monopolies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 —The Senate today passed the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2026, which seeks to strengthen efforts to combat cartels, monopolies, and other anti-competitive practices that contribute to the rising cost of living. The amendments empower the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) to deal more effectively with new tactics used by companies to evade enforcement and enhance action against anti-competitive practices, particularly those involving digital technology and the abuse of dominant market positions. “We are first addressing enforcement gaps identified throughout the implementation of the Competition Act 2010, including strengthening powers of investigation, market reviews, settlements, undertakings, and related provisions.

items.title: Muhyiddin’s trial: Company MD says he borrowed RM19.5m to donate to Bersatu at request of ‘Datuk’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — Construction company Mamfor Sdn Bhd managing director Shahradzi Shamsuddin today said a man with a “Datuk” title had in 2021 asked him to make a donation to political party Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia, as the “Datuk” would help his younger brother’s company to get a RM605.2 million government project under the Jana Wibawa programme. Shahradzi said his company Mamfor then borrowed RM19.5 million, which he donated to Bersatu using cheques, namely RM10.5 million before the project was awarded and RM9 million after the project was awarded in October 2022. Shahradzi said this while testifying as the 20th prosecution witness in Bersatu president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.

items.title: Anwar says govt studying Madani tickets for F1 race to make it more accessible
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 27 — The government is studying the possibility of introducing lower-priced MADANI tickets for the Formula One (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) to enable more people to watch the prestigious world championship, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the move was in line with the Malaysia Madani concept, which emphasised the well-being of the people and greater inclusivity in the organisation of international-scale events. “Some people have asked me, ‘PMX, will there be Madani tickets?

items.title: Anwar warns public office must never be used for personal or family gain
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — The government has a responsibility to ensure that those entrusted with public office uphold the highest standards of integrity and honesty, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Citing the case of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), which is now burdened with losses of nearly RM10 billion, Anwar said the situation was the result of failures in leadership and breaches of trust. Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief of Defence Forces General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: PM Anwar says Felda saddled with nearly RM10b losses from mismanagement and political interference
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today that the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), once the world’s largest plantation company earning billions annually, is now facing losses of nearly RM10 billion due to mismanagement and excessive political interference. According to Berita Harian (BH), Anwar said reports he received after returning to government showed Felda was saddled with debts of almost RM10 billion, forcing the administration to shoulder a heavy financial burden each year. There was excessive political interference.

items.title: Prosecution to call 25 witnesses in former Army chief’s money laundering trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — The prosecution will call 25 witnesses in the trial of former Army chief Tan Sri Muhammad Hafizuddeain Jantan and his wife, Salwani Anuar @ Kamaruddin, over charges of receiving proceeds from unlawful activities. Muhammad Hafizuddeain, 58, has been charged with six counts of receiving RM2.26 million in alleged proceeds from unlawful activities, involving deposits made into his bank accounts at various locations between Feb 2, 2024, and Nov 7, 2025. Salwani, 27, faces four charges involving the receipt of RM77,000 in alleged proceeds from unlawful activities, with the money allegedly deposited into a company-owned bank account and a bank branch in Damansara Heights, Wisma UOA II, between Nov 24, 2024, and Nov 25, 2025.

items.title: Immigration: 7,105 operations conducted, over 41,000 illegal immigrants detained this year
items.summary: KLANG, July 27 — The Immigration Department has carried out 7,105 operations, involving 96,994 inspections and the detention of 41,596 illegal immigrants nationwide as of July 15, its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said. He said enforcement under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 and the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing, Anti-Restricted Activity Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 will continue to be strengthened to ensure compliance with the Immigration Act 1959/63. He said the integrated operation, which began at about 11 am, involved 77 officers and personnel from the Immigration Department, the Labour Department and the Department of Environment.

items.title: Anthony Loke slams ‘baseless’ Adat interference claims, says rivals scapegoating DAP amid royal crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — DAP secretary general Anthony Loke has denied claims that he interfered in Negeri Sembilan’s Adat Perpatih institution, describing the allegations as baseless. According to Malaysiakini , the Chennah assemblyman said rumours linking him to the ongoing royal dispute in the state were unfounded, including suggestions that he had channelled funds to a faction opposed to Sungai Ujong chieftain Mubarak Thahak. Loke said the crisis was triggered when 14 Umno assemblymen led by Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Jalaluddin Alias withdrew their support for the Harapan led state government.

items.title: Fire breaks out at hilly forest area in Bandar Puncak Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 27 — A fire involving an estimated two-acre hilly forest area in Bandar Puncak Alam broke out this morning, with firefighting operations currently underway. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 10.06 am, prompting the deployment of a team from the Bestari Jaya Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) to the scene. Ashrul Riezal said the operation involves four personnel and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) from BBP Bestari Jaya, while PBS Saujana deployed four members to assist in controlling the blaze.

items.title: PM Anwar says Malaysia’s only cost for Bahrain F1 Grand Prix is RM16m Sepang track upgrades
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — Malaysia will not incur any registration fees from the International Automobile Federation (FIA) for hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at Sepang this October, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Formula 1 and the FIA yesterday confirmed that Malaysia will host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit, scheduled between the Azerbaijan and Singapore Grands Prix from October 2 to 4, 2026. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the only expenditure Malaysia would bear is for upgrading the Sepang track, BH reported.

items.title: Anwar says govt reviewing promotion process for senior military officers
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — The government is reviewing the promotion process for senior officers of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) to ensure their career progression is not unduly delayed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. I have asked the Chief Secretary to the Government (Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar) whether we can review the process. Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief of Defence Forces General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: New Statistics Bill aims to modernise Malaysia’s data system, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Statistics Bill 2026 is expected to be gazetted by the end of this year after completing the administrative process following its approval in Parliament, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. Akmal Nasrullah said the ministry would conduct a stakeholder engagement process after the bill is passed to enhance understanding of the importance of the new act. Commenting on the independence of official statistics from political influence, he said the Statistics Bill 2026 strengthens governance through the establishment of the National Statistics Council, which will play a role in assessing the direction and development of the country’s statistics.

items.title: Johor exco confirms Network School has not appealed, business licence revoked and operations halted
items.summary: KULAI, July 27 — The local authorities have yet to receive an appeal from the Network School for the resumption of operations following the revocation of its business licence last week. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has yet to receive an appeal application from the Network School’s representative. He said that the Network School is understood to have ceased its business operations.

items.title: IPCC receives 1,635 complaints against police since 2023, says Saifuddin
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) has received 1,635 public complaints since it began operations in 2023 up to July 24, 2026, reflecting growing public confidence in its role as an independent police oversight body. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that of the total, 844 complaints, or 76 per cent, have been resolved, while 372 complaints were received this year as of July 24. Saifuddin Nasution said the remaining unresolved complaints include cases involving complainants who were dissatisfied with the outcome of police investigations or had not received any response after lodging their complaints with the police.

items.title: Anwar says creation of Malay reserve land in KL proves commitment to Bumiputera interests
items.summary: Anwar said that after taking office in 2022, his administration moved to address the declining amount of Malay reserve land in the capital. “Since Independence in 1957, no new Malay reserve land had been created in Kuala Lumpur. “Within the area, I designated 50 acres (20 hectares) as Malay reserve land, comprising some of the most valuable land in Kuala Lumpur,” he said.

items.title: Anwar: Cabinet to decide Wednesday whether to release Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 27 — The Cabinet will decide on Wednesday whether to make public the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He said the issue would be deliberated at the weekly Cabinet meeting before a final decision is made on the report’s release. Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Armed Forces Chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: Azalina says October rulers’ meeting to decide on AG‑Prosecutor split, Cabinet backs reforms
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, said the decision to present the recommendations of the Special Select Committee regarding the amendment was made by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during a Cabinet meeting. Azalina said the Cabinet decision also covers recommendations on limiting the Prime Minister’s term of office. Earlier, in response to Abdul Halim’s initial question on the government’s institutional reform agenda, she said 21 major reform initiatives had been implemented from 2022 to 2025.

items.title: Petaling Jaya Sessions Court hears pleas as six accused face RM8m ransom kidnap charges
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 27 — Six men pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to charges of abducting a businessman and demanding RM8 million in ransom at Dataran Sunway on July 16. Berita Harian (BH) reported, A Ravichandran, 45; R Elanggovan, 45; M Jeyaraj, 43; Moses De Bretto John Patrick, 40; Ziyauddin, 33; and Muhammad Afiq Safine, 36, entered their pleas after the charges were read before Judge Dr Syahliza Warnoh. He told the court that Ravichandran supports a wife working as a clerk earning RM1,800 a month and three children; Elanggovan is the sole breadwinner earning RM1,500 monthly with a wife and three children; while Jeyaraj supports a wife and two children, BH reported.

items.title: Palace says Sultan Ibrahim’s friendship with Bahrain king paved way for F1 race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is the result of diplomatic ties and the close friendship between the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, and Bahrain’s ruler, King Hamad Isa Al Khalifa. “Since 2017, His Majesty and King Hamad have developed a good personal friendship, and this has continued to grow into a strengthening of diplomatic relations between Bahrain and Malaysia, with Sultan Ibrahim’s state visit to Bahrain in 2025. As a result, an agreement was reached to host the Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix at the Petronas SIC, where Malaysia last staged an F1 race in 2017.

items.title: Socso: Four Bentong accident victims covered under Lindung 24 Jam, families to receive long‑term support
items.summary: The next of kin of each victim are also eligible to receive the Funeral Management Benefit, amounting to RM3,000, paid as a one-time sum. “The late Alaganathan’s next of kin are also eligible for the same benefit. The organisation also confirmed that the families of the late Kanabati Raja and Parathanman have been verified as eligible to receive the Dependents’ Benefit under Lindung 24 Jam, as well.

items.title: Don’t link royalty to your campaigns, Negeri Sembilan Palace tells parties
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 27 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace today advised political parties against associating the palace or members of the royal family with their campaigns, stressing that the royal institution remains politically neutral. In a statement, the palace said any claim, statement, photograph, video or other material linking the Negeri Sembilan Palace, the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan or any member of the royal family to a political party was untrue. “The Royal Institution has always upheld the principle of neutrality and is not involved with any political party or political activity,” it said.

items.title: Chang Lih Kang says Sanusi’s comments ‘inappropriate, hurtful’, urges sensitivity during campaigns
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 27 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang has described recent remarks by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor as inappropriate and potentially hurtful to the public, urging politicians to exercise greater sensitivity, particularly during election campaigns. Chang said political leaders should be mindful of their statements to help preserve social harmony in Malaysia. On the TechnoMART Malaysia programme, Chang said RM5 billion in financing has been made available through a collaboration involving 15 organisations, including funding agencies and financial institutions, to support startups and innovators.

items.title: Body of Malaysian man killed in South Korea stabbing to be repatriated after documentation completed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — The body of a Malaysian man who died after he was allegedly stabbed during a group fight involving foreign nationals in South Korea will be brought home once documentation is completed. Family members are currently handling the repatriation process for Ahmad Shah, 26, in Eumseong County, North Chungcheong Province, according to a report by Berita Harian. Ahmad Shah was reported to have died after he was allegedly stabbed during a large brawl in South Korea.

items.title: N. Sembilan polls: Police approve 473 campaign permits, open 14 investigation papers
items.summary: Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said all approved political programmes and activities were monitored by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to ensure they complied with the law and did not jeopardise public safety or order. He said that during the same period, state police received 33 police reports and opened 14 investigation papers related to election offences. “Yesterday, police received five reports from members of the public.

items.title: Immigration raids to continue despite overcrowded detention depots, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Home Ministry (KDN) will not scale back immigration enforcement operations against foreign nationals who violate the Immigration Act 1959/63, despite the country’s 19 immigration detention depots currently operating beyond capacity. Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said enforcement efforts must continue as they are crucial to safeguarding national security and sovereignty, while ensuring foreign nationals in Malaysia comply with the country’s laws. “Malaysia is an open country.
